latin.625: ANNOTATIO V. De Manducatione Corporis Christi Orali. §. I. MANDUCATIO, actionem quandam designans, vel Propria est, vel Impropria. PROPRIA est actio Physica, seu naturalis, consistens in assumptione esculenti alicujus Corporalis, seu propriè sic dicti, in os corporis, demissioneque ejusdem in stomachum. Unde ad propriè dictam Manducationem hæc Tria, tanquam essentialia, requiruntur (1) Esculentum Corporale, ceu Objectum actionis (2) Duplex Actio Corporalis circa objectum, quarum Prior esculenti corporalis assumptione, seu receptione in os; Posterior demissione ejus in stomachum absolvitur. Utraque actio ad Manducationem propriè sic dictam, æquè necessaria: neque enim ille propriè manducare, i. e. physicè edere dicitur, qui esculentum in os solummodò recipit, mox idem ex ore emissurus, sed is demum, qui receptum in os esculentum, etiam per guttur in stomachum demittit.
latin.626: Estque vel latiùs dicta circa quodcunque esculentum propriè dictum; vel strictiùs, circa esculentum, in specie solidum, versata, quæ ex ratione soliditatis esculenti, novam specialemque actionem adsciscit, Masticationem vocatam, quâ à deglutitione distinguitur, Manducationi solidioris esculenti adeo essentialem, sive dentibus, sive gingivâ peragatur, ut etiam Manducatio, pro Masticatione, ceu pro analogo famosiori, ponatur, cibusque manducatus, non tàm comestum, quàm mansum & dentibus comminutum masticatumque cibum significet, teste Calepino. IMPROPRIA Manducatio est actio mentalis, consistens in receptione & usurpatione ejus, quô mens alitur atque perficitur, i. e. in Cognitione rerum, harumque cognitarum ruminatione, à mente instituta. Estque vel purè Mentalis, à mente, quoad naturam suam considerata, per Cognitionem rerum, naturâ noscibilium, peracta, ob id Mentalis Naturalis dicenda; vel præterea Spiritualis, à Mente per Sp. S. illuminata ac regenerata, circa res, solâ virtute Illuminationis & Regenerationis, cognoscibiles, cognoscendo & usurpando occupata, eóque Mentalis Supernaturalis nuncupanda.
latin.627: Hæc vel merè spiritualis, citra unionem cum Corporali quacunque peracta; vel insimul Sacramentalis, unitam habens Manducationem quandam à DEO injunctam Corporalem. Postremi generis est Manducatio in Cœna Sacra, utpote si legitima & talis qualis à Christo instituta, ex duplici manducatione composita ea est, Corporali nempe, & Spirituali, idque ob duplicem in S. Cœna oblatum recipiendumque cibum, spiritualem alterum seu cœlestem, Corpus nempe Domini, alterum corporalem seu terrestrem, panem, quanquam ob consecrationem extrinsecè seu relativè sacrum, i. e. à communi usu separatum. Spiritualis, quia per se & suam naturam, absque Sacramentali esse potest, uti per accidens & ob Impietatem Communicantis, Sacramentalis absque Spirituali; evenit hinc, ut Spiritualis & Sacramentalis Manducatio habeant se per modum excedentium & excessorum terminorum.
latin.628: Utraque, tam Propria, quàm Impropria, manducatio vera est, si non veritate rei significantis, tamen veritate rei significatæ. De veritate prioris Manducationis nemo ambigit; De veritate posterioris neminem sinit ambigere Sermo Christi Joh. 6. PRIOR, uti, per pleonasmum, Oralis dicitur, cùm non nisi ore fieri possit; Ita non, nisi per contradictionem, omnino negatur esse Carnalis, cùm quod orale est, eatenus, quatenus tale, non possit non carnale agnosci, ore humanô hominis carni, ex parte saltem, annumerando. Ut proinde, unô eodemque paragraphô octavô, non unâ & simplici vice lapsus deprehendatur non nemo disputans, quando tùm Supernaturalem manducationem Carnali quidem & Capernaiticæ, non item Orali, oppositam censet: quasi verò Oralis, Carnalis non esset, aut Capernaitica, saltem ex parte & quatenus Oralis est; tùm Oralem, & Veram, Manducationem, pro synonymis habet, quasi verò Spiritualis Manducatio, solâ fide peracta, non esset vera?
latin.629: Ita enim scribit: Nos (Lutherani) modum manducandi in Cœna dicimus esse Cœlestem & supernaturalem, quatenus opponitur crasso Capernaitico & carnali, non autem reali, Vero & Orali: Reformati contra cælestem & supernaturalem Manducandi modum non modò crasso & carnali, sed etiam VERO & ORALI opponunt.
latin.630: POSTERIOR, seu Impropria, in S. Cœna, Spiritualis & Supernaturalis appellanda, uti propriâ orali & carnali, quæ solius panis consecrati in Cœna est, immane quantum præstat; ita non spiritui duntaxat humano, seu hominis animæ, verùm etiam carni ejus, mediante anima, propter carnem Christi, spiritualiter, cùm extra, tùm intra Cœnam S., comestam, in beatam, ad vitam æternam, resurrectionem cedit.

pass_a.625: ANNOTATION V. On the Oral Eating of Christ’s Body. §. I. EATING, designating a certain action, is either Proper or Improper. PROPER is a Physical or natural action, consisting in the taking of some Corporal foodstuff, or foodstuff properly so called, into the body’s mouth, and the sending of the same down into the stomach. Whence for eating properly so called these Three things are required as essential: (1) Corporal Foodstuff, as Object of the action; (2) a Double Corporal Action about the object, of which the Prior is finished by taking / receiving the corporal foodstuff into the mouth; the Posterior by sending it down into the stomach. Each action is equally necessary for eating properly so called: for he is not said properly to eat, i.e. to eat physically, who only receives foodstuff into the mouth soon to emit the same from the mouth, but he only who also sends the foodstuff received into the mouth down through the throat into the stomach.
pass_a.626: And it is either more broadly so called about any foodstuff properly so called; or more strictly, concerned with foodstuff solid in kind, which from the reason of the foodstuff’s solidity takes on a new and special action called Mastication, by which it is distinguished from swallowing — so essential to the eating of solider foodstuff, whether done with the teeth or the gum, that even Eating is put for Mastication as for the more famous analog, and food eaten signifies not so much food consumed as food chewed and broken by the teeth and masticated, as Calepinus witnesses. IMPROPER Eating is a mental action, consisting in the reception and use of that by which the mind is fed and perfected — i.e. in the Cognition of things and the rumination of those known things instituted by the mind. And it is either purely Mental, performed by the mind considered as to its nature through Cognition of things knowable by nature — hence to be called Mental Natural; or moreover Spiritual, occupied by a Mind illuminated and regenerated by the Holy Spirit around things knowable by the sole virtue of Illumination and Regeneration, knowing and using them — and so to be named Mental Supernatural.
pass_a.627: This is either merely spiritual, performed without union with any Corporal eating; or at the same time Sacramental, having united with it a certain Corporal Eating enjoined by GOD. Of the last kind is Eating in the Sacred Supper — inasmuch as if legitimate and such as Christ instituted, it is composed of a double eating, namely Corporal and Spiritual, and that because of the double food offered and to be received in the Sacred Supper: the one spiritual or heavenly, namely the Lord’s Body; the other corporal or earthly, bread, though by consecration extrinsically or relatively sacred, i.e. separated from common use. The Spiritual, because by itself and its nature it can be without the Sacramental, just as by accident and from the Communicant’s Impiety the Sacramental can be without the Spiritual; hence it comes about that Spiritual and Sacramental Eating stand to each other after the manner of exceeding and exceeded terms.
pass_a.628: Each eating, both Proper and Improper, is true — if not by the truth of the signifying thing, yet by the truth of the thing signified. Of the truth of the prior Eating no one doubts; of the truth of the posterior Christ’s Discourse in John 6 lets no one doubt. The PRIOR, as by pleonasm it is called Oral, since it can be done only with the mouth; so it is denied to be Carnal only by contradiction, since what is oral, insofar as such, cannot but be acknowledged carnal, the human mouth being at least in part numbered with man’s flesh. So that in one and the same eighth paragraph someone disputing is caught slipping not once and simply, when he judges Supernatural eating opposed indeed to the Carnal and Capernaite, but not to the Oral — as if the Oral were not Carnal, or Capernaite at least in part and insofar as it is Oral; and then holds Oral and True Eating as synonyms, as if Spiritual Eating done by faith alone were not true.
pass_a.629: For so he writes: We (Lutherans) say the mode of eating in the Supper is Heavenly and supernatural inasmuch as it is opposed to the gross Capernaite and carnal, but not to the real, True and Oral: the Reformed on the contrary oppose the heavenly and supernatural Mode of Eating not only to the gross and carnal, but also to the TRUE and ORAL.
pass_a.630: The POSTERIOR or Improper eating in the Sacred Supper, to be called Spiritual and Supernatural, as it immensely surpasses the proper oral and carnal which is of the consecrated bread alone in the Supper, so it yields not only to the human spirit or man’s soul but also to his flesh, by the mediating soul, on account of Christ’s flesh spiritually eaten both outside and inside the Sacred Supper, unto a blessed resurrection to eternal life.

625: Annotatio V opens on Oral Eating of Christ’s Body. §.I: Eating is Proper or Improper.
PROPER is physical: take corporal food into the mouth and send it down into the stomach — both reception and swallowing required; mouth-only then spit-out is not proper eating.
626: Proper eating is broader (any foodstuff) or stricter (solid food needing mastication — Calepinus: ‘eaten’ often means chewed).
IMPROPER eating is mental: knowing and ruminating what feeds the mind — either Mental Natural, or Mental Supernatural when the Spirit-illuminated mind knows regeneration-things.
627: Improper spiritual eating is either merely spiritual (no corporal union) or Sacramental (joined to a God-enjoined corporal eating).

The Sacred Supper, as Christ instituted it, is of this last kind: corporal + spiritual eating for double food — Lord’s Body (heavenly) and consecrated bread (earthly). Spiritual can stand without sacramental, and (by the unworthy) sacramental without spiritual.
628: Both proper and improper eating are true (by the thing signified). John 6 settles the improper’s truth. The PRIOR / Oral cannot without contradiction be denied Carnal — the mouth is flesh.
A disputant in one §.8 slips twice: opposing supernatural only to Capernaite/carnal but not to oral, and treating Oral and True as synonyms — as if faith-alone spiritual eating were not true.
629: His Lutheran line: we call the Supper’s eating mode heavenly/supernatural as against gross Capernaite/carnal — not against real, True, and Oral.
He charges the Reformed with opposing that heavenly/supernatural mode not only to gross/carnal but also to TRUE and ORAL.
630: §.I close: the POSTERIOR / Improper eating in the Supper is Spiritual and Supernatural — far above the proper oral/carnal of consecrated bread alone.
It benefits not soul only but flesh too (soul mediating), because of Christ’s flesh spiritually eaten in and outside the Supper, unto blessed resurrection. Stop before §.II.
